dedupe_keys.name: groenblauwe netwerken knowledge bank of green blue adaptation measures

description: Groenblauwe Netwerken is a Dutch knowledge bank that helps cities choose green-blue measures for climate resilience by filtering measures to a situation and summarising what is known about their effectiveness. It covers measures across themes of water, heat, biodiversity, urban agriculture, air quality and energy, such as surface drainage and cool high-albedo materials, together with evaluated practice research and examples, and it is listed in the Dutch national climate adaptation portal as a tool for municipalities and designers. It was developed by Atelier Groenblauw, Deltares, Stichting CAS, the Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences and Hanze University of Applied Sciences, funded by the NKWK Klimaatbestendige stad research programme. The knowledge bank is available free on the web with search filters; no licence or data download is offered. Caveats: it is a web knowledge base in Dutch, and effectiveness summaries are drawn from literature, not a harmonised dataset. It supports selecting and justifying green-blue infrastructure measures in climate adaptation and stormwater planning; a related record is the Klimaateffectatlas of the Netherlands.
